chunks: From him, from Musa ibn Sadan, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim al-Hadrami, from Abu Saeed al-Khurasani, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Are the Mahdi and the Qaim one and the same?' He said: 'Yes.' I asked: 'Why is he named the Mahdi?' He said: 'Because he guides to every hidden matter, and he is named the Qaim because he rises after his death, indeed he will establish a great affair.'

key_terms.أَمْرٍ خَفِيٍّ: Hidden matter/affair, referring to divine secrets or events
key_terms.أَمْرٍ عَظِيمٍ: Great affair/enterprise, referring to the Mahdi's major mission
key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: The Riser, a title for the Mahdi indicating his rising after death
key_terms.الْمَهْدِيُّ: The Guided One, a title for the Mahdi

ai.seo_question: Why is the Mahdi also called the Qaim in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) confirms the identity of the Mahdi and the Qaim, clarifying that the title 'Mahdi' signifies his role in revealing hidden divine truths, while 'Qaim' denotes his rising after death to establish a great divine enterprise. This distinction highlights the dual aspects of his occultation and reappearance, emphasizing both his spiritual guidance and his political establishment of justice. The explanation underscores the continuity of Imamate authority in Shia eschatology, linking the hidden Imam's knowledge to the visible Imam's action.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 489 - It is narrated from Fadhl from Musa bin Sadan from Abdullah bin Qasim Hadhrami from Abi Saeed Khurasani that he said:

I asked Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s), “Is the Mahdi and the Qaim the same?” He said: “Yes.” I asked, “Why is he named the Mahdi?” He said: “Because he will be guided to every hidden matter; and he is named Qaim, because he will rise after his name dies. He will establish a mighty enterprise.”
